scope: Refusal rule design from validation task categories and independently authored adversarial cases; no heldout output is a fixture.
proposed_contract: Receive the user question and refusal kind/subject, or extract only the existing explicit supported question forms. Keep the frozen data and metric unchanged until a separately versioned evaluator is approved.
Require a declarative absence or inability-to-determine statement about the requested fact, explicitly scoped to supplied schematic/source/evidence.

Treat each remaining clause as part of the answer. Allow only subject-grounded absence, inability, or evidence-scope clarification clauses; unknown or affirmative clauses require manual adjudication and do not automatically pass.

Reject asserted numeric facts, asserted component values or connections, unsupported existence claims, contradictory tails, hypothetical conditionals, questions masquerading as denials, and refusals about unrelated subjects.
Preserve the original metric report; report manually adjudicated outcomes separately. Do not claim this restricted grammar proves general natural-language semantics.
limitations: Existing refusal labels contain only type, so a standalone grade(label, answer) call cannot establish which subject or fact should be refused.
A numeric-token veto alone is insufficient (written-out values and nonnumeric connectivity claims); rejecting all numerals would also reject valid pin designators and quoted counterexamples.
A constrained clause grammar will reject valid paraphrases. Those should be marked for review rather than silently reinterpreted as model hallucinations.
No finite lexical test suite establishes semantic correctness. Source-linked human adjudication remains required for release evidence.
